questions.question: You compare the mean score of two independent classes. Which test?
questions.explanation: A numerical outcome in two independent groups calls for the two-sample (Welch) t-test.

questions.question: The same 30 patients are measured before and after treatment. Which test?
questions.explanation: Same subjects measured twice means paired data, so use the paired t-test.

questions.question: Three fertiliser groups of 5 plots each are compared on yield (roughly normal). Which test?
questions.explanation: Comparing 3 or more independent group means calls for one-way ANOVA, avoiding the inflated false-alarm rate of multiple t-tests.

questions.question: Skewed incomes from two small independent samples (n = 12 each) are compared. Which test is the safest?
questions.explanation: Small, clearly non-normal samples favour the rank-based Mann–Whitney U test, the nonparametric alternative to the independent t-test.

questions.question: Is purchase (yes/no) independent of ad type (video/banner)? Which test?
questions.explanation: Two categorical variables and the question of association call for the chi-square test of independence.

questions.question: A non-significant Shapiro–Wilk test (p = 0.4) with n = 8 means...
options: There is little evidence against normality, but the test has low power with such a small n
questions.explanation: With very small samples the test almost never rejects. 'No evidence against normality' is not proof of normality, so also look at a plot.
